To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The arena was a success in the sense that it enabled knowledge sharing, but the knowledge sharing was limited to the pilot project.

(a) the arena for energy efficient building was successful in bringing together researchers and practitioners in a joint project; (b) this joint project was successful in facilitating knowledge sharing and collaborative interaction between the different professional groups involved; and

(1) the arena was a successful arena for sharing knowledge, (2) knowledge sharing was mainly achieved within a pilot project, (3) knowledge sharing was facilitated by the mutual willingness of researchers and practitioners to adapt and attempt translating the disciplinary discourses, (4) knowledge sharing was enabled by the participants’ expectations of, and investments in, the arena activities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how knowledge sharing and learning can be facilitated between actors that normally would not meet in their daily practice.
how knowledge sharing between various research organisations and municipal actors may be facilitated.
the development of arenas for cleaner production and how such arenas can be used for knowledge sharing between different disciplines and professional groups.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

knowledge is shared through interaction and that interaction is dependent on the willingness of the individuals to adapt and translate the disciplinary discursive and communicative modes of the others.
the arena was successful in facilitating knowledge sharing between the actors involved, but that this knowledge sharing was limited to those who were directly engaged in the arena’s activities.
the arena has had a positive impact on knowledge sharing and learning across the different professional and organisational boundaries.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
knowledge sharing and learning across organisational boundaries is a social process and is dependent on the individuals’ motivation and willingness to adapt their professional practice.
the arena is a promising approach to facilitate the development and implementation process of energy efficient renovation projects.

knowledge-sharing is a complex social process, which requires mutual willingness and motivation, as well as a certain level of flexibility in terms of adapting to the different professional cultures and practices.
The main takeaway from our work is that

in order to enhance knowledge sharing and collaborative learning, it is important to facilitate the translation of disciplinary discourses, and to create a common language and a common frame of reference.
the arena approach can be a fruitful means for enhancing knowledge exchange across professional boundaries and disciplines.

knowledge-sharing is not only dependent on the individual’s willingness and ability to share and receive knowledge, but also on the individual’s motivation for sharing knowledge and the context in which the interaction takes place.
